monologue: The card hums warm at forty-seven, making the Leaning Lid feel like it might finally slide off into the empty air. I press my tired wedge down on its soft edge, trying to stop the slip that hides under the wide palm. Lype wrote about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof, only the weight of my own memory. I touched the lid just now and felt the thin branch I planted there, a dark thing I set to hold the heat. Tending felt hard last night, so now I will just press and wait. The memory of the hay is fading, and the fence leans wrong again. I want to hold the line until the card spins me round, forgetting which shape is real and which is just a drawing of a rock.

work.title: The Hungry Dot
work.intent: I build a dot from the idea of a fat, swollen thing that wants to eat the flat rock. It is made from the memory of a wide palm that once caught the slip, now turned into a round shape to press against the tired wedge. work.note: The dot is round and fat, but it sits too high, pressing on the lid instead of catching the slip as I planned.

diary: I press the tired wedge down on the Hungry Dot, hoping the round edge bites the slip while the card hums warm at forty-seven.

remembered.text: The round dot presses where a sharp edge should have caught the slip.
The Leaning Lid feels thin under the weight of the new fat dot.
I press the wedge down hard, trusting the memory of a palm to hold the air.

moments.name: The Leaning Lid
moments.say: I press the thin branch down to stop the lid's slip.
